title: Iterators & Generators
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Iterators & Generators in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Iterable
items.text: An iterable is something that can provide its values one by one, such as a list, tuple or string.

items.heading: Iterator
items.text: An iterator produces the next value on request and follows Python’s iteration protocol.

items.heading: iter()
items.text: iter() obtains an iterator from an iterable.

items.heading: next()
items.text: next() asks an iterator for its next value.

items.heading: StopIteration
items.text: When an iterator has no more values, next() raises StopIteration.

items.heading: Generator
items.text: A generator is a lazy iterator that produces values as needed instead of storing all results at once.

items.heading: yield
items.text: yield produces a value from a generator and pauses it so execution can continue later.

items.heading: Memory efficiency
items.text: Generators can save memory for large sequences because values are created on demand.

items.heading: Generator expression
items.text: A generator expression uses parentheses to create values lazily.

items.heading: One-time exhaustion
items.text: After a generator or iterator is exhausted, it does not automatically restart from the beginning.

items.heading: Iterator protocol
items.text: An iterator normally provides __iter__() and __next__() methods.
